messages:
maria: heads-up — SkylinePay POC started hitting streaming failures during the demo. customer noticed frequent SSE disconnects and partial JSON chunks, causing the client to throw parse errors.

skyline-engineer: yeah, saw it. their frontend shows 'Unexpected end of JSON input' after a few seconds of stream. happens more under heavy prompts.

sanjay: do we have any server-side logs for the timeframe? which deployment (hosted/dedicated/private)?

maria: hosted API region-us-west2, model=redwood-2-xl, route=/v1/stream. I'll paste a snippet from their client console and our logs.

skyline-engineer: client log: `SSE connection opened` -> chunks arrive -> then `event: data\ndata: {"id":"resp_abc","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Hello"}` -> disconnect -> `Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input` on parse.

maria: server trace (shortened):
```
2026-03-18T15:04:12Z INFO connection accepted id=conn-7f9
2026-03-18T15:04:12Z INFO stream chunk sent id=resp_abc size=512
2026-03-18T15:04:13Z WARN transient socket close client=skyline-ip ttl=1
2026-03-18T15:04:13Z ERROR stream terminated id=resp_abc reason=client_disconnect
```

alex: two quick suspects: 1) intermediary proxy (Skyline infra or corporate proxy) cutting connections based on idle or chunk size; 2) our chunk framing + nginx/timeouts causing truncated final event.

kate: also check our SSE keepalive: are we sending colon-heartbeat `: keepalive\n\n` periodically? some browsers/proxies drop otherwise.

maria: our payloads do include `: ping` every 20s, default. but their disconnects are within 2–5s.

eng-oncall-bot: @maria — recent platform deploy to streaming router at 2026-03-18T14:58Z changed chunk flush behavior (enable_coalescing=true). Rollback was not triggered.

sanjay: that flag might cause larger aggregated chunks but also different socket flush timing. for client-side partial JSON parse, might be that our last SSE event is missing the terminating "\n\n" sequence when connection drops mid-flush. skyline frontend likely does naive parse per event and expects complete JSON.

skyline-engineer: their frontend is a simple parser: `ev.data && JSON.parse(ev.data)` — no streaming decoder.

alex: temporary mitigations for the POC: 1) turn off coalescing for their tenant (force immediate flush per token), 2) increase keepalive interval to 5s to detect broken pipes faster, 3) add server-side event terminator enforcement so we never emit a truncated JSON event (finalize before flush).

maria: can eng do tenant-scoped flip? we have feature flag for streaming.coalesce per-tenant. if so we can set it to false and ask Skyline to retry.

eng-oncall-bot: feature flag `streaming.coalesce` found. current value: `true` for org=skylinepay. Change requires a rolling config push to the router (no restart).

sanjay: I can push the change — will take ~2–3min to propagate. Doing it now.

sanjay: pushed streaming.coalesce=false for org=skylinepay. please try repro.

skyline-engineer: re-ran demo, still seeing a disconnect but now payloads are smaller — less partial JSONs, but we got a case where two events merged: `}{"id":"resp_xxx"` causing JS parse error because client concatenates events before parse.

kate: that suggests client-side concatenation is fragile. we should recommend Skyline use a resilient SSE client: parse per `\n\n` boundary and handle incremental chunks, or use a streaming JSON parser. but for POC we should avoid sending adjacent JSON events without proper delimiting.

alex: we can also add a simple mitigation: prefix every event with a `data: ` and ensure we never send `}{` at the boundary by inserting a zero-width separator in between events (or a newline). but that's hacky. better: ensure we always emit `\n\n` between events and flush before closing.

maria: action items:
- eng: ensure router enforces event terminator and flush semantics for tenant (sanjay + alex)
- devex: provide Skyline integration note for robust SSE parsing (kate)
- sales: update POC notes and ask customer to test behind their proxy (maria)

sanjay: quick patch pushed to router to add explicit event terminator on final chunk and disable coalescing for tenant. monitoring now.

maria: Skyline retested — demo ran for 12 minutes with continuous stream, only one brief reconnection (automatic retry) and no parse errors reported. they still asked about recommendations for production (rate limits, retries).

kate: for prod recs: use exponential backoff reconnects, idempotent resume token in SSE (we have `X-Stream-Resume` header support in Dedicated+Hosted), and prefer our SDK which handles partial frames and JSON assembly. I'll send a short snippet they can drop in: 
```
// minimal resilient client
const source = new EventSource(url);
let buffer = '';
source.onmessage = e => {
  buffer += e.data;
  try {
    const obj = JSON.parse(buffer);
    buffer = '';
    // handle obj
  } catch (err) {
    // wait for more data
  }
};
```

maria: good. Skyline wants a follow-up run tomorrow at 10:00 PST. I'll include the config changes and the client snippet. also asked about pricing impact of disable-coalescing on token cost.

alex: disabling coalescing increases per-token overhead slightly (more small writes) — negligible for POC, but for sustained high-throughput we recommend enabling batching and using KV prefix caching. I'll add numbers: ~3–5% token compute overhead in synthetic tests.

maria: thanks everyone. I'll close this thread after follow-up. :thumbsup:

skyline-engineer: thanks, team — appreciate the rapid triage. will ping if anything else pops up.
